newsitem.title: LEBANON: Iraqi opposition group claims attack on Uday.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi opposition group claims attack on Uday.

text.p: A Tehran-based Iraqi opposition group said on Friday that it was behind the assassination attempt against President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday in Baghdad.

"A group of our heroic strugglers...inflicted the verdict of God and the people unto the enemy of God and the people, Uday Saddam al-Tikriti, who has caused mischief and crime in the land, like his dictator father," the Islamic Dawa Party said in a statement faxed to an international news agency in Beirut.

The group said in the statement dated December 12 that its fighters "besieged (Uday's) motorcade at al-Mansour market in Baghdad on Thursday afternoon and fired a hail of bullets, wounding him several times, so he escaped from a certain death".
Uday's car was attacked by gunmen as he drove on Thursday evening in Baghdad's smart al-Mansour disctrict.
Eyewitnesses said at least two gunmen attacked Uday's car, injuring the 32-year-old along with several bystanders. Uday was reported to be in a Baghdad hospital.
Iraqi authorities are investigating the attempt to kill Uday, official Iraqi media reported on Friday, wishing him a quick recovery from his wounds which were said to be not serious.
Uday heads Iraq's National Olympic Committee and is also head of the Iraq Soccer Federation. He owns Iraq's most influential newspaper Babel.
Uday holds a degree in engineering and military studies.
President Saddam Hussein has two sons and three daughters.
